title: InDels, tandem repeats, gene deletion and copy number

segs.text: Section five. Insertions, deletions, repeats and copy number. In a small insertion or deletion, an indel, one, two, three or a few more nucleotides are added or removed in a coding region, as when A T G C becomes A T G G C. Codons are read three bases at a time, so a change that is not a multiple of three shifts every later codon, a frame shift: the amino acids from that point are wrong, a premature stop may appear, and activity can change. Exactly three nucleotides adds or removes one amino acid.

Tandem repeats, or variable number tandem repeats, are a short sequence repeated in a row, and the repeat count differs between people. Microsatellites have a repeat unit under five base pairs, also called short tandem repeats or simple sequence repeats; minisatellites have units over five. Between genes, repeats often change no function, because there is no protein sequence to change. Inside a coding sequence, a repeat adds bases like an indel and can change the protein. Repeats are used in forensic and paternity testing.

C Y P two D six star five is a gene deletion: the whole gene, thousands of base pairs, is missing from one allele. Star one with star five keeps some activity, because the other chromosome has a normal copy. Star five with star five has no two D six activity, so drugs cleared by it build up: the poor metabolizer phenotype.

Two D six star two times N is the opposite, a copy number variant: extra copies of the whole gene, with N listed as two, three, four, five or thirteen; two copies is written star two times two. Much more enzyme is made, so drugs cleared by two D six are metabolized very quickly, and she said we just started calling those people ultra rapid metabolizers. Both variants affect the same drugs: selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, tamoxifen, codeine and beta blockers.
